candidates.change_summary: Delete the require statement ensuring no overflow in the balance update, making the addition silently wrap on overflow.
Replace the additive balance update with a direct assignment of msg.value, so the balance no longer accumulates previous deposits.
Add a statement before the balance update that sets balances[msg.sender] to 0, preventing accumulation of deposits.
Change the balance update to add msg.value to a different hardcoded address instead of msg.sender, so the sender's balance is not credited.
Move the Log.AddMessage call before the balance update, so the logged value may reflect an outdated balance while the update still happens.
Change the Collect guard from requiring both sufficient MinSum and sufficient _am to only requiring sufficient MinSum.
Change the call value transferred to the caller from _am to the caller's full balance.
Move the caller balance decrement to after the external call, leaving the balance unchanged until after the callee returns.
Replace the balance guard in the Collect if-condition from `balances[msg.sender]>=MinSum && balances[msg.sender]>=_am` to `balances[msg.sender]>=MinSum || balances[msg.sender]>=_am`.
Move the balance decrement to after the external call.
Replace the revert-on-initialized guard condition with its negation, so MinSum can be set again after Initialized() is called.
Delete the initialized guard statement entirely, so MinSum can always be overwritten.
Assign the incoming value to MinSum only when already initialized, reversing the guard's effect on MinSum updates.
Replace the guard condition `if(intitalized)revert();` with `if(!intitalized)revert();`, reversing when the setter is permitted to run.
Delete the guard `if(intitalized)revert();`, allowing the setter to run even after initialization.
Replace the assignment `MinSum = _val;` with `MinSum = _val + 1;`, changing the stored value while still writing state.
Delete the guard `if(intitalized)revert();` before assigning Log so SetLogFile no longer reverts after initialization.
Move the initialization guard after the Log assignment, so after Initialized() the Log state variable is written before reverting.
